reading.title: Why Real English Sounds Harder
reading.intro_zh: 本文不复述课文，而是从认知科学角度讲“为什么真实口音的英语比课堂英语更难听懂”：内容改编自 NIH/PMC 收录的同行评审论文 Listening effort and accented speech（Frontiers in Human Neuroscience, 2014）。

source.title: Listening effort and accented speech
source.publisher: Frontiers in Human Neuroscience (via NIH/NCBI PMC)

passage: Many language learners share a frustrating experience: after years of careful study, they finally meet a real speaker and suddenly cannot follow a single sentence. Researchers in cognitive neuroscience argue that this gap is not a sign of failure but a predictable consequence of how the brain processes unfamiliar speech. When someone speaks with an accent that differs from the listener's expectations, the incoming sounds no longer match the patterns stored in memory. This mismatch forces the brain to work harder, and the resulting strain is known as listening effort.

Crucially, an accent does not have to be unintelligible to be demanding. Even when learners eventually grasp every word, studies show that decoding an unfamiliar accent demands more time and places a heavier load on the mind than listening to the voices typically encountered in a classroom. Because mental capacity is limited, this extra burden has downstream costs: listeners may understand a message yet struggle to remember it afterwards, or fail to manage another task while concentrating on the unfamiliar voice. The effort, in other words, is invisible but real.

There is, however, genuine reason for optimism. Researchers emphasize that listening effort lies on a spectrum rather than being fixed. A mild accent, or one a person has encountered repeatedly, can be understood almost effortlessly. Through a process called perceptual adaptation, the brain gradually recalibrates its expectations after sustained exposure, so that voices which once seemed bewildering eventually feel ordinary. The difficulty a traveller feels on arrival is therefore temporary, dissolving steadily as the ear learns to decode the rhythms of real speech.

questions.question: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Language teachers should speak with strong regional accents.
Learners who cannot follow real speech have wasted their study time.
Unfamiliar accents are harder to process because of how the brain handles speech, but adaptation is possible.
Foreign accents are always impossible for listeners to understand.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文主旨是：陌生口音之所以难懂，是因为大脑处理语音的机制（听力努力），但通过适应可以改善；并非学习失败，也不是永远听不懂。

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens when a speaker's accent differs from the listener's expectations?
options: The incoming sounds no longer match the patterns stored in memory.
The listener immediately forgets their own language.
The speaker automatically slows down to help.
The brain stops processing the speech entirely.
questions.explanation_zh: 第一段说，当口音与听者预期不同，传入的声音不再匹配记忆中储存的模式，于是大脑必须更费力。

questions.question: Why can accented speech cause problems even when the listener understands every word?
options: Because the words are translated into another language first.
Because the speaker refuses to repeat anything.
Because classroom voices are deliberately confusing.
Because the extra cognitive effort can make the message harder to remember or leave less capacity for other tasks.
questions.explanation_zh: 第二段指出，即使听懂了每个词，处理带口音的语音会更慢并占用额外认知资源；由于脑容量有限，可能记不住内容，或无法同时兼顾其他任务。

questions.question: What can we infer about a traveller who keeps hearing the same local accent for several weeks?
options: They will permanently lose the ability to understand their teacher.
They will gradually find that accent easier to understand.
They will need to study grammar all over again.
They will stop being able to speak their first language.
questions.explanation_zh: 第三段提到“感知适应”：持续接触后大脑会重新校准预期，原本难懂的口音会逐渐变得平常，所以反复听同一口音会越来越好懂。

questions.question: In the final paragraph, the word "recalibrates" is closest in meaning to which of the following?
options: completely forgets
loudly repeats
adjusts and resets
permanently blocks
questions.explanation_zh: recalibrate 意为“重新校准/调整”。文中说大脑在长期接触后逐渐 recalibrates its expectations，即重新调整、重置自己的预期，故选 adjusts and resets。

writing.intro_zh: 今天把四个结构提升到 B2+：问路求助、强调自己已尽力表达、用 neither...nor... 描述听力困难的原因，以及在真实交流中礼貌地请求重复——都用更抽象、更书面的语境来仿写。

patterns.title: did not know the way to ...
patterns.source: I did not know the way to my hotel, so I asked a porter.
patterns.focus_zh: 用 the way to... 表示“去某地的路”，后面自然接 so I asked... 说明你怎么求助。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句（更抽象的语境）：在一个陌生而拥挤的环境里你找不到去某处的路，于是向某位工作人员求助，并说明原因。
must_include: did not know the way to
patterns.sample: Overwhelmed by the crowded terminal, I did not know the way to the departure gate, so I asked a uniformed attendant for directions.
patterns.tip_zh: the way to 后面接地点，比只说 where is... 更有叙事感。

patterns.title: not only... but... as well
patterns.source: I not only spoke English very carefully, but very clearly as well.
patterns.focus_zh: 这个结构把两个优点放在一起，表示“我已经很努力了”。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句（更抽象的语境）：在一次重要的交流中，你不但在某一方面很努力，而且在另一方面也同样用心，以此强调你已尽全力。
patterns.sample: During the interview I not only articulated each point carefully, but rephrased my main argument patiently as well, hoping to be understood.
patterns.tip_zh: A 和 B 最好是同一类动作或特点，比如 carefully / clearly / politely / slowly。

patterns.title: neither... nor...
patterns.source: He answered me, but he spoke neither slowly nor clearly.
patterns.focus_zh: neither... nor... 一次否定两个方面，很适合描述“听不懂”的原因。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句（更抽象的语境）：对方虽然回应了你，但其表达既不清晰也不连贯，从而解释了你为何难以理解。
patterns.sample: The official eventually responded to my enquiry, but he spoke neither slowly nor clearly, which left me genuinely struggling to follow.
patterns.tip_zh: neither 后面和 nor 后面要放并列成分，比如两个副词 slowly / clearly。

patterns.title: Could you say that again, please?
patterns.source: I am a foreigner. Could you say that again, please?
patterns.focus_zh: 真实交流中，比硬撑更重要的是礼貌地请求重复或放慢速度。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句（更抽象的语境）：在正式或陌生的场合，你坦承自己听力吃力，并礼貌地请求对方放慢速度或重复关键信息。
patterns.sample: I am still adjusting to the local accent, so I wonder, could you possibly repeat that last instruction more slowly, please?
patterns.tip_zh: Could you...? 加 please 很适合旅行、车站、酒店前台等礼貌求助场景。
